title: The Mid-Autumn Festival
description: Four recordings about the Mid-Autumn Festival: making lanterns, a school announcement, a story and a family tradition.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · Making a lantern
parts.intro: You will hear Linh and Nam making lanterns.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Nam, look! I'm making a star lantern for the festival. Do you want to help me?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Yes, please. What do we need?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Red and yellow paper, glue, and a small candle. Well, not a real candle. My mum says it's not safe, so we'll use a little electric light.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: That's a good idea. I made a fish lantern last year, but it was too heavy and it broke.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: This one is easy. We need five points for the star. Can you cut the paper? I'll put on the glue.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Sure. Is your grandmother coming to see it?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Yes, she's coming on Thursday evening. She's bringing some moon cakes, too.

parts.title: Part 2 · A school announcement
parts.intro: You will hear Mr Hung talking about the school lantern parade.

script.speaker: Mr Hung
script.text: Good morning, students. Here is some news about our Mid-Autumn lantern parade. It's on Thursday evening, and we start at six o'clock.

script.speaker: Mr Hung
script.text: Please meet at the school gate. We will walk to the park, which takes about twenty minutes.

script.speaker: Mr Hung
script.text: There will be a lantern competition. The best lantern wins a big box of pencils. The teachers will decide.

script.speaker: Mr Hung
script.text: At seven o'clock, there will be a lion dance in the park, and everyone can eat moon cakes and fruit.

script.speaker: Mr Hung
script.text: Parents are welcome, but small children must stay with an adult. Please bring a warm jacket. It can be cool at night.

parts.title: Part 3 · Grandpa's story
parts.intro: You will hear Mai asking her grandfather about the moon.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Grandpa, can you tell me the story of the moon again?

script.speaker: Grandpa
script.text: Of course, Mai. Long ago, there was a boy called Cuoi. He found a magic tree, and he looked after it very carefully.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: What happened to the tree?

script.speaker: Grandpa
script.text: One day, it began to grow up into the sky, and Cuoi held on to it. He went all the way to the moon, and he lives there still.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Can we see him tonight?

script.speaker: Grandpa
script.text: Look carefully at the moon. Some people say you can see a boy under a tree. I think it looks like a rabbit, but that's only my idea.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: I think I can see the boy! He looks very happy.

script.speaker: Grandpa
script.text: Yes, and he's not alone. Children everywhere look at him at this time of year.

parts.title: Part 4 · My family's festival
parts.intro: You will hear Ms Hoa talking about how her family celebrates the festival.

script.speaker: Ms Hoa
script.text: In my family, the Mid-Autumn Festival is the best night of the year. We start in the afternoon, when my mother makes sweet soup.

script.speaker: Ms Hoa
script.text: We put a big tray on the table with fruit, tea and moon cakes. There are many kinds of moon cakes. My favourite has lotus seeds inside, but my brother likes the ones with egg.

script.speaker: Ms Hoa
script.text: When the moon comes up, we all go outside to see it. It is very round and bright on this night.

script.speaker: Ms Hoa
script.text: The children walk around the garden with their lanterns and sing songs. The smallest child gets the first piece of cake.

script.speaker: Ms Hoa
script.text: We usually go to bed late, but nobody minds. It is a night for families to be together.
